newsitem.title: CANADA: Doman CEO allowed to remain pending appeal.
newsitem.headline: Doman CEO allowed to remain pending appeal.

text.p: Doman Industries Ltd chief executive Herb Doman will be allowed to remain in his position while he seeks an appeal of his conviction on insider-trading charges, his lawyer said Tuesday.

The British Columbia Court of Appeal granted Doman a stay of charges that temporarily freezes a British Columbia Securities Commission ruling that ordered Doman to step down by Oct 1. and banned him from trading securities for 10 years.
Lawyer Marvin Storrow who represents Doman said the penalties were stayed pending arguments before the court on whether Doman should be allowed to appeal in the case.

The case grew out of the collapse in 1988 of a takeover bid for Doman by Louisiana-Pacific Corp. Doman was accused of tipping the Bennett brothers off about the deal's demise before it was disclosed publicly. They sold their shares and reaped a C$2 million profit.
The court is expected to hear those arguments in about five weeks, he said.

Doman, former British Columbia premier William Bennett and his brother Russell Bennett were found guilty of insider trading in August after an eight-year legal battle. The three were banned from securities trading for 10 years and from serving as directors or officers of public companies.
They were also ordered to pay costs in the case.
Doman was to be allowed to return to his position as head of his lumber company in a year if certain conditions were met.
